This eliminates all corruption risk by never mutating the original log's causal stream.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The use case requires strict run-level continuity (e.g., regulatory audit trails that demand a single run identity).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The new run cannot access the prior log as structured input, losing causal context.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The overhead of spawning a new run is prohibitive for the workload.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The system's identity model does not support cross-run references.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Even with clean halts and checkpoints, resumption conflates two causal episodes (pre-halt and post-halt) under a single run identity, risking subtle corruption from environmental drift, configuration changes, or non-determinism accumulated during the pause. A new run with a fresh identity that cites the prior log as input preserves the original log's append-only identity absolutely, while the new log's identity is independently clean. The cost is losing run-level continuity, but the benefit is eliminating an entire class of corruption modes.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
